title: RGB BODYWORKS: a car paint shop puzzle where colors mix as light, so you can solve it by hex code (free, browser)
author: office-canard
selftext:
RGB BODYWORKS is a free puzzle game set in a car body shop. You can play it in the browser.



Play: [https://office-canard.itch.io/rgb-bodyworks](https://office-canard.itch.io/rgb-bodyworks)



An order comes in with a color sample. You pour paint from cans into the spray guns to mix that exact color and amount, with nothing left over. Get it wrong, and the color still goes on the real car. Then cars with mismatched doors line up and honk at you. That's my favorite part.



Why light, not paint



It started with paint. Then I thought about universal design: people see color very differently. If the colors mix as light (red, green and blue), every color can be written as a hex code. So a player who can't rely on color can still play it as a hex arithmetic puzzle. It also works as practice for young people who want to be designers. And the colors you mix are the same system every screen in the world uses, so you might look at your monitor a little differently afterward.



1000 stages, with 60s-70s country music on the radio.



How AI fit in



\- Code: Claude wrote all of it in plain JavaScript, about 1,200 lines, Canvas 2D and Web Audio, no libraries.

\- Art: Gemini drew the base car (one grey sedan), the backgrounds, the shelves and signs, the title art and the icon. Claude split the car into a paint layer and part masks in code, so the paint you mix is applied in code. Cans, beakers, spray guns and color samples are drawn in code.

\- Music: Claude wrote 6 country tunes and plays them live with 11 instruments from the FluidR3 GM soundfont (MIT). Drums are synthesized.

\- Sound effects: all 5 are synthesized with Web Audio. Claude made candidates on a test page, and I picked them by ear.

\- Stages: a generator builds puzzles by actually pouring, so every one is solvable. They're scored by a model of how people solve them, then ordered. The first 8 teach one thing at a time. 

\- Testing: a script replays the stored solution of all 1000 stages, move by move, and checks every gun ends up with the ordered color and amount and nothing is left over.

\- The idea of switching from paint to light was mine.



Feedback welcome, especially if you play it by hex code.
